title: See the repetition
prompt: Join orders to order_items, then show the joined row count as joined_rows and the number of different orders as real_orders. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS joined_rows, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS real_orders FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS joined_rows, COUNT(o.id) AS real_orders FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS joined_rows FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id;

title: How many orders per customer, correctly
prompt: Show each customer_id and their number of orders, as orders, after joining to order_items. Repeats must not inflate the count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS orders FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;
SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(i.order_id) AS orders FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;

title: Summarise first
prompt: Show each customer_id and total units as units. Use a subquery in FROM to total units per order, then join to orders.
hints: Summarise order_items, then join the summary.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(t.units) AS units FROM orders o JOIN (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) t ON t.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS units FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS units FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

title: Students in a subject
prompt: Show each subject and how many different students took it, as students. A retake mustn't count twice.
hints: Join to courses, then count distinct students.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT c.subject, COUNT(DISTINCT e.student_id) AS students FROM enrolments e JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY c.subject;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.subject, COUNT(*) AS students FROM enrolments e JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY c.subject;
SELECT c.subject, COUNT(DISTINCT e.course_id) AS students FROM enrolments e JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY c.subject;

title: Inflated salaries
prompt: Each department's total salary is wanted, but with a second table joined it can double. Show each department_id and its true total as total, from employees joined to departments once.
hints: This join is safe, as each employee matches one department.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT e.department_id, SUM(e.salary) AS total FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY e.department_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.department_id, SUM(e.salary) AS total FROM employees e JOIN departments d GROUP BY e.department_id;
SELECT e.department_id, COUNT(e.salary) AS total FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY e.department_id;

title: Fix the inflated total
prompt: This should show how many different customers bought each product, as buyers, but it counts every purchase. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT i.product_id, COUNT(o.customer_id) AS buyers
FROM order_items i
JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id
GROUP BY i.product_id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 9, 1, NULL), (13, 9, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT i.product_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS buyers FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id GROUP BY i.product_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT i.product_id, COUNT(o.customer_id) AS buyers FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id GROUP BY i.product_id;
SELECT i.product_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.order_id) AS buyers FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id GROUP BY i.product_id;

title: Average order size
prompt: Show the average units per order as avg_units, rounded to 2 decimals. Add up units first, then average those totals.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT ROUND(AVG(units), 2) AS avg_units FROM (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(quantity), 2) AS avg_units FROM order_items;
SELECT ROUND(SUM(quantity), 2) AS avg_units FROM order_items;

title: Spend by city
prompt: Show each customer city and total revenue as revenue (price times quantity), and the number of different orders as orders.
hints: Revenue sums item rows, and order count needs DISTINCT.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.city, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.city;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.city, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue, COUNT(o.id) AS orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.city;

SELECT c.city, SUM(p.price) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.city;
